hints: Look at the name ethyl butanoate and remember how an ester name splits into its two parent parts.
The first part of the name comes from the alcohol and the second part comes from the acid, so identify which acid has 4 carbons and which alcohol has 2 carbons.
Write the 1 to 1 esterification equation and use moles to link 2.32 g of ester with $M_r = 116$ to the mass of water with $M_r = 18$.
walkthrough:
**Split the ester name**

Think of an ester as acid part + alcohol part. The ending tells you the acid, the beginning tells you the alcohol.

$$\text{ethyl butanoate} = \text{ethyl (from ethanol)} + \text{butanoate (from butanoic acid)}$$

**Identify the correct reactants**

Butanoic acid is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ with 4 carbons. Ethanol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ with 2 carbons.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \rightleftharpoons \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Calculate moles of ester formed**

The formula of ethyl butanoate is $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_2$, so $M_r = (6 \times 12) + 12 + 32 = 116$.

$$n(\text{ester}) = \frac{2.32}{116} = 0.0200 \text{ mol}$$

**Link to mass of water**

Esterification makes 1 mol of water for every 1 mol of ester, so moles of water is also 0.0200 mol.

$$m(\text{H}_2\text{O}) = 0.0200 \times 18 = 0.36 \text{ g}$$

**Choose the matching row**

Only the row with butanoic acid plus ethanol and 0.36 g of water has both parts correct.

options.A: Correct. Butanoic acid provides the C4 butanoate part and ethanol provides the C2 ethyl part. 0.02 mol of ester forms 0.02 mol of water, giving 0.36 g.
options.B: The reactants are correct but the mass is wrong. 0.40 g comes from a calculation error, often using $M_r = 20$ for water or miscalculating moles of ester. The correct 1:1 mole ratio gives 0.36 g.
options.C: The mass 0.36 g is correct but the reactants are swapped. Ethanoic acid (C2) plus butan-1-ol (C4) would make butyl ethanoate, not ethyl butanoate. Remember the alcohol gives the first word, the acid gives the second.
options.D: Both parts are wrong. Ethanoic acid plus butanol makes the isomeric ester butyl ethanoate, and 0.40 g does not match the mole calculation for 2.32 g of ester.
